answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small stake in a shared vault before it may transact, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues only through completed work verified by independent peers, like light through a crystal: one fake facet is easy to spot against the whole. A new agent starts with a walnut-sized trust budget that grows only as it delivers, so an attacker must spend real effort to gain real influence.
